curation.deployment_topology: A local NoneBot project constructs an Alconna command and lets the plugin apply global command prefixes before matcher evaluation.
curation.observed_behavior: The corrected single-header fixture accepts slash, hash, and empty prefixes; the reported failure remains only when Alconna receives a list containing two command headers, where slash and hash no longer match.
curation.expected_behavior: If list-valued command headers are supported with global command_start, every header should receive the configured prefixes consistently.
required_evidence_gaps: An authoritative contract for list-valued Alconna command headers combined with alconna_use_command_start at the reported version.
A maintainer diagnosis or fixing commit that distinguishes unsupported construction from a prefix application defect.
An isolated fixture without unrelated project matchers that demonstrates the remaining multi-header behavior.
ruled_out: The original claim that alconna_use_command_start fails for a single string header; the reporter's corrected fixture says that form works.
unknowns: Whether the list-valued header form was a supported public contract in Alconna 0.41.0.
Why the reporter closed the issue without a linked fix or maintainer resolution.

curation.deployment_topology: NapCat reports the bot's own OneBot V11 message_sent event to a NoneBot process containing multiple Alconna matchers.
curation.observed_behavior: The generic OneBot Event initially fails an isinstance(MessageEvent) assertion; after the closing commit accepts its message_id, the reporter still observes repeated rule-check failures because event.get_message() raises ValueError('Event has no message!').
curation.expected_behavior: A self-message report is either normalized or ignored without repeated Alconna rule exceptions, while normal message events remain matchable.
required_evidence_gaps: The commit or released version that handles the second Event has no message failure after the closing commit.
A deterministic message_sent event fixture proving that all Alconna matchers terminate without repeated rule exceptions.
Evidence separating a true event feedback loop from many independent matchers logging the same unsupported event.
ruled_out: message_id is absent; the reporter confirmed getattr(event, 'message_id') returns a value.
The closing commit alone fully resolves the reported behavior; a later comment shows a different exception in the same path.
unknowns: Whether the complete behavior was fixed in a later unlinked commit or release.
Whether NapCat's generic message_sent event shape is guaranteed by the supported adapter contract.
